title: CELPIP General Listening — Practice Test 15
instructions: Listen to the audio for each part and answer the questions. Each audio plays once.

parts.title: Problem Solving
parts.description: A conversation in which one person has a problem and seeks help from another.

parts.title: Daily Life Conversation
parts.description: An everyday conversation between two people.

parts.title: Listening for Information
parts.description: An informational talk; listen for specific details.

parts.title: Discussion
parts.description: A discussion among people with different viewpoints.

parts.title: Viewpoints
parts.description: A longer talk presenting one speaker's opinion and reasons.

listeningScripts.title: A Deposit Held Back
listeningScripts.text: Caller: I moved out three weeks ago, and I've had a letter saying two hundred dollars is being kept back from my deposit for cleaning. The flat was cleaner when I left it than when I moved in. Agent: I can look at the file. What is the address? Caller: Fourteen Ashgrove, unit six. Agent: Right. I have the move-out inspection here. It says oven requires professional clean, and carpet marked in the second bedroom. Caller: There was no mark on that carpet when I left. And I did clean the oven. Agent: Was there a move-in inspection? That is the document that matters here. Caller: There was. We walked round with the previous manager and he filled in a form. Agent: Then that form should be on the file, and I am not seeing it. If the move-in report is missing, the landlord can't establish what condition the flat was in when you took it on, and a deduction for damage needs a before as well as an after. Caller: What about the oven, though? That is cleaning, not damage. Agent: Cleaning is a different test. They can charge for cleaning only to bring it back to the standard it was at move-in, not to make it better than it was. So if the move-in form said the oven was already marked, that is the end of it. Caller: I took photographs on the day I moved in. Time-stamped. Agent: Those are worth more than the form, honestly. Send them with a written request for the deposit, and give a deadline. Fourteen days is standard. Caller: And if they refuse? Agent: Then it is the tenancy board, and the filing fee is fifty dollars, which you get back if you win. But most of these settle once photographs appear, because the landlord can see how it is going to go.

listeningScripts.title: Sorting Out a Carpool
listeningScripts.text: A: Are you still driving in every day? B: Four days. I work from home on Wednesdays. A: Because I'm on the same road, and I'm paying nine dollars a day to park. B: Then let's share. I'd take the passenger seat gladly. My licence renewal is stuck in the post somewhere. A: You can't drive at all? B: I can drive. I just can't produce the card if anybody asks, which for a month is fine and for six months isn't. A: So I drive, and you pay half the parking. B: Half the parking and half the fuel. That's fair, and I'd rather it were fair than cheap, because otherwise one of us resents it by March. A: Agreed. What time do you need to be in? B: Half eight. I can stretch to nine. A: I'm a quarter to eight person. That's the problem. B: Then that's the deal. I come in at your time and I use the extra forty-five minutes. It's the quietest part of my day anyway. A: And if one of us is ill? B: We tell each other the night before, not the morning of. Anything after seven and I'm already committed to the bus.

listeningScripts.title: Library Makerspace Induction
listeningScripts.text: Right. Everybody here has booked the induction, and you need it before you can book anything in the room at all. It lasts an hour, and it does not have to be repeated unless you have been away more than two years. The three-D printers first. Booking is in two-hour blocks, and you can hold two bookings at a time and no more, because a handful of people were holding a week each. Print material is provided for the first hundred grams a month; after that you bring your own, or buy a spool at the desk. What you cannot do is set a print running and go home. Somebody has to be in the building — not in the room, but in the building — because a failed print is a smoke alarm about one time in two hundred. The laser cutter needs a separate sign-off, which is a second session, and there is a materials list on the wall. Read it. It is not a list of what works. It is a list of what is safe: PVC in a laser cutter gives off chlorine gas, and that is why you cut what is on the list and nothing else, even if you have watched somebody online do otherwise. The sewing machines need no sign-off at all. Take them, use them, and put the bobbin case back the way you found it. Files: bring them on a USB stick, or use your library account. Do not email them to staff, because the staff address strips attachments over ten megabytes, and you will think it has arrived when it hasn't. And the room closes half an hour before the library does, not at the same time. Every week somebody discovers that at eight o'clock.

listeningScripts.title: Ice Road Season Shortened
listeningScripts.text: The Northwest Territories has put back the planned opening of its winter ice roads by three weeks, after warm weather in November left the ice too thin to carry heavy loads. The route to the northern communities will now open in mid-January rather than late December, and the department has cut the maximum load from sixty-four thousand kilograms to forty-four thousand for the first month. Ice roads carry the year's fuel, building materials and bulk food to communities that have no all-weather road, and anything not delivered inside the window has to be flown in. Freight costs about seven times as much by air. A supply company said the shortened season will mean between forty and sixty additional flights, and warned that some construction planned for next summer will not go ahead, because the materials cannot arrive in time. The department said it will not extend the season at the other end, because the spring melt is less predictable than the freeze and the risk is not symmetrical.

listeningScripts.title: An Artificial Pitch
listeningScripts.text: Duguay: The field is unusable from November to April. An artificial pitch gives us eleven months instead of five, and the quote is one point four million. Ferrero: Eleven months is right, and it is the single thing that would change my season. We lose eight fixtures a year to that ground being under water. Achebe: I want to know what happens to it in July. The last artificial pitch I stood on was fifty-two degrees at the surface in the sun, and the school has no shade at all on that side. Ferrero: You water it. Achebe: With what? We are on restrictions two summers in three. Duguay: There is a cooler infill. Cork rather than rubber crumb, and it is about eighty thousand more. Achebe: Then I would want that specified, not offered as an upgrade that disappears when the tender comes back over budget. Duguay: Fair. Specified. Ferrero: My worry is the replacement. These surfaces last eight to ten years and then you are buying another one, and nobody ever puts that in the business case. Duguay: This one does. There is a sinking fund of ninety thousand a year in the proposal. Ferrero: Ninety times ten is nine hundred thousand. And the replacement is what, a million? Duguay: Closer to eight hundred, because the base stays. You are only replacing the carpet. Achebe: Then the number works, as long as the fund is ring-fenced and cannot be borrowed against for a roof. Duguay: I can't promise a future board won't touch it. I can put it in the motion.

listeningScripts.title: Requiring Supermarkets to Donate Unsold Food
listeningScripts.text: France did this in twenty-sixteen, and other countries have looked at it since. The law says a supermarket over a certain size may not throw away edible unsold food, and must have an agreement with a charity to take it. It sounds unanswerable. I want to explain why the results are smaller than the headline, and still worth having. Start with the arithmetic that never makes the news. Supermarkets are not where most food waste happens. In most countries households throw away several times what retailers do — the figure I would stand behind is that retail is somewhere under a tenth of the total. So a law that covers the retail slice perfectly still leaves the large majority of the problem untouched. Second, a good deal of what gets donated was already being donated. The better chains had arrangements before the law, because it saves them the disposal cost. What the law actually reaches is the tail — the chains that could not be bothered. The tail is real, but it is a tail. Third, and this is the part where I have changed my mind: the binding constraint is usually not the supermarket's willingness. It is the charity's cold chain. A pallet of chilled food arriving at six in the evening at a food bank with one van and one fridge is not food. It is a problem. Where these laws worked, money went in alongside the mandate — refrigerated vans, staff, storage. Where the mandate was passed on its own, donations rose and so did the amount thrown away by the charities. So I support it, with a condition that is not optional. Mandate the donation and fund the receiving end in the same bill. A mandate on its own moves the waste one step down the chain and calls that a solution.

questions.prompt: Why is the caller telephoning?
options: She has been billed for repairs after moving out
Her deposit has not been returned at all
Part of her deposit is being kept back for cleaning
She has been asked to pay for a professional cleaner
questions.correctAnswer: Part of her deposit is being kept back for cleaning
questions.explanation: The caller has had a letter keeping two hundred dollars of the deposit back for cleaning, which she disputes.

questions.prompt: What does the move-out inspection record?
options: An oven needing a professional clean and a marked bedroom carpet
A marked carpet in every room
An oven that had been damaged
Cleaning that was left unfinished throughout
questions.correctAnswer: An oven needing a professional clean and a marked bedroom carpet
questions.explanation: The inspection lists two things: the oven requiring a professional clean, and a carpet marked in the second bedroom.

questions.prompt: Which document does the agent say matters most?
options: The signed tenancy agreement
The move-out inspection report
The letter withholding the deposit
The move-in inspection report
questions.correctAnswer: The move-in inspection report
questions.explanation: The agent asks straight away whether there was a move-in inspection, calling it the document that matters, and then cannot find it on the file.

questions.prompt: Why does the missing form help the caller?
options: A missing form voids the tenancy agreement
A deduction for damage needs a record of the condition beforehand
The landlord must return the deposit within fourteen days
The inspection has to be repeated with the tenant present
questions.correctAnswer: A deduction for damage needs a record of the condition beforehand
questions.explanation: Without the move-in report the landlord cannot establish what condition the flat was in at the start, and a damage deduction needs a before as well as an after.

questions.prompt: What is the test for a cleaning charge?
options: It may be charged whenever a professional clean is needed
It applies only if the tenant did no cleaning at all
It may only restore the standard the flat was in at move-in
It is treated in the same way as damage
questions.correctAnswer: It may only restore the standard the flat was in at move-in
questions.explanation: The agent distinguishes cleaning from damage: a landlord may charge to bring the flat back to its move-in standard, not to improve on it.

questions.prompt: What does the agent say is worth more than the form?
options: A statement from the previous manager
The photographs taken on the day she moved in
The move-out inspection
A letter from the tenancy board
questions.correctAnswer: The photographs taken on the day she moved in
questions.explanation: Told about the time-stamped photographs, the agent says they are worth more than the form and should go with the written request.

questions.prompt: What deadline does the agent suggest?
options: Fourteen days
Three weeks
Fifty days
The end of the month
questions.correctAnswer: Fourteen days
questions.explanation: The agent advises sending the photographs with a written request for the deposit and setting a deadline, of which fourteen days is standard.

questions.prompt: Why do most of these cases settle?
options: The filing fee is more than the amount in dispute
The tenancy board decides most cases against landlords
Landlords must pay the tenant's costs if they lose
Once photographs appear, the landlord can see how it will go
questions.correctAnswer: Once photographs appear, the landlord can see how it will go
questions.explanation: The agent says most settle once photographs appear, because the landlord can see how the case is going to go — the fifty-dollar fee is returned to the tenant if they win.

questions.prompt: Why does A raise the subject?
options: A's car is due to be replaced
A is paying nine dollars a day to park
A dislikes driving in traffic
A works the same hours as B
questions.correctAnswer: A is paying nine dollars a day to park
questions.explanation: A brings it up because they travel the same road and A is paying nine dollars a day for parking.

questions.prompt: Why would B rather not drive?
options: B does not have a car
B finds the route difficult
B's insurance has lapsed
B's renewed licence has not arrived
questions.correctAnswer: B's renewed licence has not arrived
questions.explanation: B can drive but cannot produce the card, because the licence renewal is stuck in the post — tolerable for a month, not for six.

questions.prompt: What does B offer to pay?
options: Half the parking only
A fixed sum each month
Half the parking and half the fuel
Nothing, in exchange for driving on Wednesdays
questions.correctAnswer: Half the parking and half the fuel
questions.explanation: B offers half of both, saying it should be fair rather than cheap.

questions.prompt: Why does B want the arrangement to be fair rather than cheap?
options: Otherwise one of them will come to resent it
A would otherwise refuse to drive
The parking receipt has to be split exactly
B expects fuel prices to rise
questions.correctAnswer: Otherwise one of them will come to resent it
questions.explanation: B's reason is that an unfair arrangement leads to one of them resenting it by March.

questions.prompt: What is the rule if one of them is ill?
options: Take the bus without telling the other
Telephone before seven in the morning
Pay the other's parking for that day
Tell the other the night before rather than that morning
questions.correctAnswer: Tell the other the night before rather than that morning
questions.explanation: B sets the rule at the night before, because anything after seven leaves B already committed to the bus.

questions.prompt: When must the induction be taken again?
options: After an absence of more than two years
Every two years, without exception
Before each separate piece of equipment
Only if the equipment changes
questions.correctAnswer: After an absence of more than two years
questions.explanation: The induction lasts an hour and need not be repeated unless somebody has been away for more than two years.

questions.prompt: How many printer bookings may a person hold at once?
options: One
Four
Two
As many as are free
questions.correctAnswer: Two
questions.explanation: Bookings run in two-hour blocks and a member may hold two at a time and no more, a limit introduced after some people held a week each.

questions.prompt: Why must somebody stay in the building during a print?
options: The printers must be restarted between layers
A failed print sets off a smoke alarm roughly once in two hundred
The room is locked from the outside
Print material runs out without warning
questions.correctAnswer: A failed print sets off a smoke alarm roughly once in two hundred
questions.explanation: The rule is that somebody has to be in the building, though not in the room, because roughly one failed print in two hundred sets off a smoke alarm.

questions.prompt: What is the materials list beside the laser cutter for?
options: It lists what the library sells at the desk
It shows which materials need a sign-off
It records what each member has cut
It says what is safe to cut, not what cuts well
questions.correctAnswer: It says what is safe to cut, not what cuts well
questions.explanation: The speaker is emphatic that it is not a list of what works but of what is safe — PVC, for instance, gives off chlorine gas in a laser cutter.

questions.prompt: Which equipment needs no sign-off?
options: The sewing machines
The three-D printers
The laser cutter
Everything, once the induction is done
questions.correctAnswer: The sewing machines
questions.explanation: The sewing machines need no sign-off at all; the laser cutter needs a second session, and the printers require the induction.

questions.prompt: Why should files not be emailed to staff?
options: Staff cannot open files sent from home
Files must be checked before they are printed
Anything over ten megabytes is stripped before staff see it
The library account is faster than email
questions.correctAnswer: Anything over ten megabytes is stripped before staff see it
questions.explanation: Emailed files may silently fail, because the staff address strips attachments above ten megabytes and the sender believes it has arrived.

questions.prompt: What has happened to the ice road season?
options: It has been cancelled for this winter
It has been extended into the spring
It has been opened three weeks early
Its opening has been put back by three weeks
questions.correctAnswer: Its opening has been put back by three weeks
questions.explanation: The opening moves from late December to mid-January, three weeks later than planned.

questions.prompt: Why has this happened?
options: A shortage of maintenance crews
November was warm enough to leave the ice too thin
Damage to the route from last year's traffic
An unusually early spring melt
questions.correctAnswer: November was warm enough to leave the ice too thin
questions.explanation: Warm November weather left the ice too thin to carry heavy loads, which is what forced the delay.

questions.prompt: What has changed about the loads?
options: The maximum falls from sixty-four to forty-four thousand kilograms
The maximum rises for the first month only
Fuel may no longer be carried at all
Loads are unchanged but journeys are fewer
questions.correctAnswer: The maximum falls from sixty-four to forty-four thousand kilograms
questions.explanation: For the first month the department has cut the maximum load from sixty-four thousand kilograms to forty-four thousand.

questions.prompt: How much more does air freight cost?
options: About twice as much
About forty per cent more
About seven times as much
About sixty times as much
questions.correctAnswer: About seven times as much
questions.explanation: Anything not delivered in the ice road window has to be flown in, and freight costs about seven times as much by air.

questions.prompt: Why will the season not be extended in spring?
options: The communities have asked for an earlier close
The melt is less predictable than the freeze
The route is needed for summer construction
Extending it would cost more than the flights
questions.correctAnswer: The melt is less predictable than the freeze
questions.explanation: The department says the risk is not symmetrical: the spring melt is less predictable than the freeze, so the season will not be lengthened at that end.

questions.prompt: What is Duguay's case for the pitch?
options: A saving of one point four million over ten years
Eleven usable months a year instead of five
Fewer injuries on a level surface
The field cannot be repaired any longer
questions.correctAnswer: Eleven usable months a year instead of five
questions.explanation: Duguay opens with the field being unusable from November to April, against eleven months of use from an artificial pitch, at a quote of one point four million.

questions.prompt: What does Ferrero say the school loses now?
options: Eight weeks of training each winter
Most of its home games in the spring
Eight fixtures a year to a waterlogged ground
The use of the field for five months
questions.correctAnswer: Eight fixtures a year to a waterlogged ground
questions.explanation: Ferrero supports the case with a specific figure: eight fixtures a year lost to the ground being under water.

questions.prompt: What is Achebe's concern?
options: How hot the surface becomes in summer
That the pitch will be used by outside clubs
That the quote excludes floodlighting
That the field is the only green space left
questions.correctAnswer: How hot the surface becomes in summer
questions.explanation: Achebe raises July: the last artificial pitch she stood on reached fifty-two degrees at the surface, and that side of the school has no shade.

questions.prompt: Why is watering not an answer to that?
options: Watering damages the artificial surface
The school has no supply on that side
It would cost more than the cooler infill
The area is under water restrictions two summers in three
questions.correctAnswer: The area is under water restrictions two summers in three
questions.explanation: Ferrero suggests watering; Achebe answers that they are on restrictions two summers in three.

questions.prompt: What does Duguay offer in response?
options: Shade planting along that side of the school
A cork infill costing about eighty thousand more
A summer closure of the pitch
A reduction in the overall quote
questions.correctAnswer: A cork infill costing about eighty thousand more
questions.explanation: Duguay raises a cooler infill — cork instead of rubber crumb — at about eighty thousand dollars more.

questions.prompt: What does Achebe insist on about the infill?
options: That it be tested before the tender goes out
That the extra cost come from the sinking fund
That the supplier guarantee the surface temperature
That it be written into the specification rather than offered as an upgrade
questions.correctAnswer: That it be written into the specification rather than offered as an upgrade
questions.explanation: Achebe wants the cork specified, so that it cannot quietly disappear when the tender comes back over budget — and Duguay agrees.

questions.prompt: What is Ferrero's other worry?
options: That the pitch will be unusable in heavy rain
That fixtures will be moved to other schools
The cost of replacing the surface after eight to ten years
That the eleven-month figure is optimistic
questions.correctAnswer: The cost of replacing the surface after eight to ten years
questions.explanation: Ferrero points out that these surfaces last eight to ten years and that the replacement is usually left out of the business case.

questions.prompt: Why does the sinking fund cover the replacement?
options: Only the carpet is replaced, not the base beneath it
The fund earns interest over the ten years
The replacement is due after fifteen years, not ten
A grant covers the difference
questions.correctAnswer: Only the carpet is replaced, not the base beneath it
questions.explanation: Ferrero's arithmetic gives nine hundred thousand against a replacement he guesses at a million; Duguay puts it closer to eight hundred, because the base stays and only the carpet is renewed.

questions.prompt: What does the law require?
options: All shops must give unsold food away free to customers
Charities must collect from every supermarket daily
Larger shops must have an agreement with a charity rather than bin edible food
Supermarkets must reduce the food they order
questions.correctAnswer: Larger shops must have an agreement with a charity rather than bin edible food
questions.explanation: The law prevents a supermarket above a certain size from throwing away edible unsold food and requires an agreement with a charity to take it.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say the retail slice is small?
options: Households waste several times more food than shops do
Most supermarket food is sold before it expires
Retail waste is counted differently in each country
Supermarkets already donate most of their surplus
questions.correctAnswer: Households waste several times more food than shops do
questions.explanation: In most countries households waste several times what retailers do, and the speaker puts retail somewhere under a tenth of the total.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say the law actually reaches?
options: The largest supermarkets, which waste the most
Households, indirectly, by changing what shops stock
Charities, by giving them a legal right to the food
The chains that had made no arrangement before
questions.correctAnswer: The chains that had made no arrangement before
questions.explanation: The better chains already had arrangements, because donating saves disposal costs; what the law reaches is the tail of chains that could not be bothered.

questions.prompt: What has the speaker changed his mind about?
options: That the law is worth having at all
That the real obstacle is the charity's cold chain
That households are the larger source of waste
That charities would rather have money than food
questions.correctAnswer: That the real obstacle is the charity's cold chain
questions.explanation: The speaker names this as the point where he changed his mind: the binding constraint is not the supermarket's willingness but the receiving charity's refrigerated capacity.

questions.prompt: What happened where the mandate was passed on its own?
options: Supermarkets found ways around the requirement
Charities refused to sign the agreements
Donations rose, and so did what charities threw away
The law was repealed within a few years
questions.correctAnswer: Donations rose, and so did what charities threw away
questions.explanation: Where money went in alongside the mandate the law worked; where the mandate stood alone, donations rose and so did the amount the charities discarded.

questions.prompt: What condition does the speaker attach to his support?
options: The law should apply to households as well
The receiving end must be funded in the same bill
Supermarkets should be paid for what they donate
The size threshold should be lowered
questions.correctAnswer: The receiving end must be funded in the same bill
questions.explanation: The speaker supports the law only if the donation mandate and the funding of the receiving end arrive together, since a mandate alone moves the waste one step down the chain.
